summary: Ruflo appears to be a workflow/flow-orchestration technology. We evaluated it as an intelligence source only (no runtime use) and extracted patterns and capabilities that MITIGATE can assimilate natively. We recommend treating Ruflo as an assimilation candidate for ideas and patterns while avoiding any runtime dependency.

recommendation.rationale: Score indicates maturity and usefulness. We prefer native assimilation to preserve MITIGATE core and provider independence. Risks (licensing, supply chain, plugin execution) are manageable when not adopting the runtime.

mitigate_capabilities_snapshot: Task execution framework with structured deterministic outputs

core: DAGs with conditional branches and loops
Retries with exponential backoff and jitter
Plugin/extension mechanism for tasks and hooks
differentiators: Dynamic graph mutation based on runtime data
Dry-run planning and diff of planned vs. actual
gaps_vs_mitigate: First-class Flow DSL with schema and validation
Pluggable executor registry with capability discovery

useful_for_mitigate: Event-sourced state machine to track run lifecycle
Retry/backoff with bounded retries and jitter
Circuit breakers and bulkheads for external calls
Plugin discovery via declarative entry points
anti_patterns_to_avoid: Hidden global mutable state between tasks
Unbounded fan-out without quotas or limits

security: Execution of untrusted plugins/tasks can lead to RCE
Privilege escalation if runners share credentials

concerns: License compatibility with MITIGATE’s distribution is unknown
Third-party plugin licenses may be more restrictive
Transitive dependency licenses may introduce copyleft obligations
actions: Obtain and review Ruflo core license and NOTICE
Inventory transitive dependencies and their licenses
Confirm compatibility with MITIGATE’s chosen license
Require SPDX identifiers and license scanning for any copied code

dependencies: Runtime lock-in to Ruflo DSL and state store
Unclear release cadence and maintenance posture
Potential breakage from rapid minor releases
Migration and data portability if format changes
operational: State corruption or partial checkpoints on crash
Non-determinism across retries or parallel branches
Orphaned or zombie runs after worker failure
Resource contention/memory leaks in long-lived workers

native: Define MITIGATE FlowSpec v1 (YAML/JSON) with JSON Schema
Implement deterministic runner with durable checkpoint store
Introduce IdempotencyKey decorator and storage-agnostic interface
Design TaskRegistry plugin API with capability discovery
Add DryRun planner to produce execution plan/diff artifacts
Standardize secrets redaction and provenance on outputs
near_term: Add Checkpointer interface with file/kv backends
Generate flow visualizations from FlowSpec for docs/CLI
Introduce StructuredResult type with metadata and redaction
Add per-step deadlines and cancellation semantics
long_term: Optional web timeline/graph UI driven by stored runs

notes: Do not import or execute Ruflo code; reimplement patterns natively
Keep storage and execution adapters provider-agnostic
Expose stable JSON contracts to avoid vendor lock-in

provider_independence.assessment: Maintained by avoiding Ruflo runtime and using standard interfaces/adapters only

test_plan: JSON Schema validation for FlowSpec documents
Property-based tests for idempotency and replay safety
Security tests ensuring secrets never appear in logs/artifacts
Load tests verifying concurrency limits and backpressure
acceptance_criteria: No runtime or build-time dependency on Ruflo
All new components have 90%+ unit test coverage
FlowSpec schema and examples pass validation and linting
Idempotency and retry semantics are deterministic and documented
Security review completed; redaction proven in tests

unknowns_and_assumptions: We did not install or execute Ruflo; features are inferred from typical workflow/orchestration systems and limited public descriptions.
Exact licensing, dependency tree, and security posture are unknown and must be verified during human review.
Data model/storage format and observability integrations are not confirmed.
Any assimilation will preserve MITIGATE core design and avoid vendor lock-in.
